Levelized cost of capture To calculate the estimated levelized cost of capture (LCOC), the capital and O&M costs were used, and the methodologies established in the DOE NETL baseline reports30, 31 were followed. The levelized capture cost was estimated, applying the global economic assumptions in Table 15. The current capture cost is approximately $612.25 per tonne of CO₂. As shown in Table 19, the dominant contributor to this cost is the fixed operating expenses, with a significant share coming from operating labor. If the plant capacity is increased while maintaining the same number of personnel, the fixed labor cost would be distributed over a larger amount of CO₂ captured. This would reduce the fixed-cost contribution per tonne and therefore lower the overall capture cost. For example, if the plant productivity were doubled to approximately 6,000 tonne/year while maintaining the same number of operating laborers, the estimated capture cost would decrease by $117/tonne, assuming a linear increase in other costs.
